requirements.evidence: All contract routes in routes/web.php:19-42 with correct names, methods, guest/auth/verified/signed/throttle:6,1 middleware. Login rate limit per lower(email)+IP, auth.failed/auth.throttle on email, Session::regenerate + intended(home) (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:24-44,47-63). Register uses the exact key str()->transliterate('register|'.ip), 5 tries, Registered event, login, regenerate (Register.php:27-56). Password::defaults set once (AppServiceProvider.php:24). Reset rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset (PasswordResetController.php:51-58). EmailVerificationRequest gives 403 on tampered id; send() skips already-verified users (EmailVerificationController.php:31-38). User implements MustVerifyEmail; .env.example and phpunit.xml pins are present; ui.php exists in both locales with 'Entrar', 'Senha', 'Esqueceu a senha?'. Gaps: e-mail is validated with plain 'email' (no strict/rfc mode) in Login.php:26, Register.php:41 and PasswordResetController.php:23,46, although the task asks for strict validation; 'Bulma CSS' and the colour sample are still hardcoded in welcome.blade.php.

conventions.evidence: Livewire components validate with inline arrays in $this->validate([...]) (Login.php:25-28, Register.php:39-43) instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern. No tests at all, which breaks the mandatory TDD rule. No CHANGELOG.md or docs update. On the plus side: Bulma markup, {{ }} escaping, route() everywhere, wire:model plain, inline $request->validate in controllers, and User keeps its #[Fillable] attribute.

security.evidence: CSRF on all forms, session invalidate + regenerateToken on logout (SessionController.php:12-16), session regenerated on login/register, rate limiting in both Livewire actions, throttle on the forgot, verify and resend routes, signed verification URL, remember_token rotated on reset, no {!! !!}. Minor points: the forgot-password User::where(...)->exists() pre-check (PasswordResetController.php:27) adds a timing difference between existing and missing e-mails. E-mail validation is not strict.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files: nothing under tests/ for login, register, throttling, reset, verification tamper (403), localization, or Livewire unauthorized/tamper calls, even though conventions.md requires tests for every feature.

simplicity.evidence: Lean controllers and components that reuse Laravel primitives (Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest, redirectGuestsTo/redirectUsersTo). Small redundancies: the User::where(...)->exists() check before Password::sendResetLink, which already handles unknown users (PasswordResetController.php:27); `$email ?? request()->query('email')` in reset-password.blade.php:17, which duplicates the controller's edit(); and the layout serves both @yield('content') and $slot (layouts/app.blade.php:37-38).

readability.evidence: Clear names and short methods (ensureIsNotRateLimited, throttleKey). Views are consistent and translation keys are well organised. The leftover commented `// use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\MustVerifyEmail;` stays next to the new real import (User.php:5-7). Public methods have no PHPDoc.

scope.evidence: Mostly on task. Unrelated edits: removed the @fonts directive from welcome.blade.php, reworded the welcome page copy and added CTA buttons, and added a jsdelivr Bulma CDN fallback in the new layout (layouts/app.blade.php:13).

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests for any requirement (login, throttling, register, reset, verification tamper 403, localization), which violates the mandatory TDD convention and the Livewire definition of done.
The Livewire components validate with inline rule arrays instead of the project's #[Validate] attributes on public properties.
The task asks for strict e-mail validation, but the code uses the plain 'email' rule rather than e.g. 'email:rfc,strict'.
There is no CHANGELOG or docs update for a major new feature, although the docs-sync convention requires one.
The redundant existence pre-check runs extra work only for existing users, which opens a timing side channel. The broker already handles unknown e-mails silently.
'Bulma CSS' is still hardcoded screen text despite the rule that all text comes from translation files.
The @fonts directive was removed and the welcome page copy and layout changed, which the task did not ask for.
The `?? request()->query('email')` fallback duplicates what the controller already passes.
The stale commented-out MustVerifyEmail import was left beside the real import.

review.summary: The change implements session auth with Livewire login/register, password reset, e-mail verification, logout and pt_BR/en UI translations. The routes and the security mechanics (rate limiting, session regeneration, signed verification, remember_token rotation) are largely correct. It ships no tests at all, which breaks the mandatory TDD convention, and it skips the project's #[Validate] pattern and docs/CHANGELOG updates, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
